Claude Code runs as a CLI on a server, but sometimes you want to talk to it from a phone or tablet — devices that can’t run a terminal. This app bridges that gap: it wraps a local Claude Code process behind a web interface that any browser on the network can reach.

The claude-agent-sdk (official Python SDK) handles the heavy lifting: it spawns Claude Code as a subprocess and communicates via JSON over stdin/stdout. Our job is to expose that over HTTP with real-time streaming, keep the auth token alive, and provide a usable mobile-friendly UI.

Dependencies

quart
claude-agent-sdk
requests

The flake provides a dev shell with all Python dependencies. Packages available in nixpkgs (quart, requests) come from there; claude-agent-sdk is fetched from PyPI via buildPythonPackage. The SDK bundles its own claude CLI binary, which is the one the app always uses — no separate npm install needed.

The shebang in app.py uses this flake: nix develop .../remoteclaude --command python3, so ./app.py just works for local debugging.

{
  inputs.nixpkgs.url = "github:NixOS/nixpkgs/nixos-unstable";

  outputs = { nixpkgs, ... }:
    let
      forAllSystems = f: nixpkgs.lib.genAttrs
        [ "x86_64-linux" "aarch64-linux" ]
        (system: f nixpkgs.legacyPackages.${system});
    in {
      devShells = forAllSystems (pkgs:
        let
          arch = pkgs.stdenv.hostPlatform.linuxArch;
          claude-agent-sdk = pkgs.python3Packages.buildPythonPackage rec {
            pname = "claude_agent_sdk";
            version = "0.1.50";
            src = pkgs.fetchurl {
              url = "https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/py3/${builtins.substring 0 1 pname}/${pname}/${pname}-${version}-py3-none-manylinux_2_17_${arch}.whl";
              hash = "sha256-ST2MxD9BZikWBnSc9HsD6CLwO383HMd69pdWQBfM9Xk=";
            };
            format = "wheel";
            dependencies = with pkgs.python3Packages; [ anyio mcp ];
            doCheck = false;
            dontAutoPatchelf = true;
            dontStrip = true;
            dontFixup = true;
          };
          py = pkgs.python3.withPackages (ps: [
            ps.quart
            ps.requests
            claude-agent-sdk
          ]);
          claude-code = pkgs.stdenv.mkDerivation rec {
            pname = "claude-code";
            version = "2.1.81";
            src = pkgs.fetchurl {
              url = "https://registry.npmjs.org/@anthropic-ai/claude-code/-/claude-code-${version}.tgz";
              hash = "sha256-h1rMZyQalKYiC1WXEq/wssImRYUHZIwwjHPJeIvEWy8=";
            };
            nativeBuildInputs = [ pkgs.makeWrapper ];
            unpackPhase = "tar xzf $src --strip-components=1";
            installPhase = ''
              mkdir -p $out/lib/claude-code $out/bin
              cp -r . $out/lib/claude-code/
              makeWrapper ${pkgs.nodejs}/bin/node $out/bin/claude \
                --add-flags "$out/lib/claude-code/cli.js"
            '';
          };
        in {
          default = pkgs.mkShell {
            packages = [ py claude-code ];
            CLAUDE_CLI = "${claude-code}/bin/claude";
          };
        });
    };
}

The hash above is a placeholder — nix will tell you the correct one on first build. To get it:

cd nomad/files/remoteclaude && nix develop 2>&1 | grep 'got:'

Verifying frontend dependencies

The frontend loads Tailwind CSS and Alpine.js from a CDN. Before upgrading either package, run this script to verify the file is identical across three independent sources: the npm registry tarball, jsdelivr, and unpkg. If a package was compromised at the registry level, all three would match (they all mirror npm), but a CDN-level or DNS-level attack would show a mismatch — which is the more likely attack vector.

The script outputs the SRI hash to paste into the integrity attribute.

set -euo pipefail

tmp=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT

# 1. npm registry tarball (authoritative source)
curl -sL "https://registry.npmjs.org/${pkg}/-/$(basename "$pkg")-${ver}.tgz" \
  | tar xzf - -C "$tmp"
hash_npm=$(sha384sum "$tmp/package/$file" | awk '{print $1}')

# 2. jsdelivr CDN
curl -s "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/${pkg}@${ver}/${file}" > "$tmp/jsdelivr"
hash_jsdelivr=$(sha384sum "$tmp/jsdelivr" | awk '{print $1}')

# 3. unpkg CDN
curl -sL "https://unpkg.com/${pkg}@${ver}/${file}" > "$tmp/unpkg"
hash_unpkg=$(sha384sum "$tmp/unpkg" | awk '{print $1}')

if [ "$hash_npm" = "$hash_jsdelivr" ] && [ "$hash_npm" = "$hash_unpkg" ]; then
  sri=$(echo "$hash_npm" | xxd -r -p | base64 -w0)
  echo "OK  ${pkg}@${ver} — all 3 sources match"
  echo "SRI sha384-${sri}"
else
  echo "MISMATCH for ${pkg}@${ver}!"
  echo "  npm:      $hash_npm"
  echo "  jsdelivr: $hash_jsdelivr"
  echo "  unpkg:    $hash_unpkg"
  exit 1
fi

OK  @tailwindcss/browser@4.2.1 — all 3 sources match
SRI sha384-YjO+ErKeO4iVSG6ZwntywbAuZEVdO8EUm0+Yav33kSZtDQzFoa5K3bA2EmTWcUYq

OK  alpinejs@3.15.8 — all 3 sources match
SRI sha384-LXWjKwDZz29o7TduNe+r/UxaolHh5FsSvy2W7bDHSZ8jJeGgDeuNnsDNHoxpSgDi

Wiring it up

The SDK is fully async, so we need an async web framework. Quart (async Flask) lets us await the SDK directly in request handlers without threading hacks.

This section sets up everything the app needs before it can serve requests. The goal is that the app can start on a headless server and keep itself authenticated indefinitely without human intervention — or shout for help when it can’t.

import asyncio
import json
import os
import re
import secrets
import sys
import time
import uuid

import requests as http_requests
from quart import Quart, Response, render_template, request, jsonify
from claude_agent_sdk import query, list_sessions, get_session_messages, ClaudeAgentOptions
from claude_agent_sdk.types import (
    StreamEvent, AssistantMessage, ResultMessage, TextBlock,
)

os.environ.pop("CLAUDECODE", None)

_current_query_task = None

app = Quart(__name__)
CREDENTIALS_PATH = os.path.join(os.path.expanduser("~/.claude"), ".credentials.json")


def write_credentials(oauth):
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(CREDENTIALS_PATH), exist_ok=True)
    with open(CREDENTIALS_PATH, "w") as f:
        json.dump({"claudeAiOauth": oauth}, f)


def read_credentials():
    try:
        with open(CREDENTIALS_PATH) as f:
            return json.load(f).get("claudeAiOauth")
    except (FileNotFoundError, json.JSONDecodeError):
        return None
VAULT_ADDR = os.environ.get("VAULT_ADDR", "http://127.0.0.1:8200")
ROLE_ID = os.environ.get("ROLE_ID")
SECRET_ID = os.environ.get("SECRET_ID")

_vault_token = None


def vault_login():
    global _vault_token
    r = http_requests.post(
        f"{VAULT_ADDR}/v1/auth/approle/login",
        json={"role_id": ROLE_ID, "secret_id": SECRET_ID},
    )
    r.raise_for_status()
    _vault_token = r.json()["auth"]["client_token"]


def vault_headers():
    return {"X-Vault-Token": _vault_token}


def vault_renew():
    r = http_requests.post(
        f"{VAULT_ADDR}/v1/auth/token/renew-self",
        headers=vault_headers(),
        json={"increment": "1h"},
    )
    if r.status_code == 403:
        vault_login()


def vault_read(key):
    vault_renew()
    r = http_requests.get(
        f"{VAULT_ADDR}/v1/secret/data/remoteclaude/{key}",
        headers=vault_headers(),
    )
    if r.status_code == 200:
        return r.json()["data"]["data"]
    return None


def load_credentials_from_vault():
    vault_login()
    creds = vault_read("creds")
    if not creds:
        return False
    oauth = dict(creds)
    if "expiresAt" in oauth:
        oauth["expiresAt"] = int(oauth["expiresAt"])
    if isinstance(oauth.get("scopes"), str):
        oauth["scopes"] = json.loads(oauth["scopes"])
    write_credentials(oauth)
    return True
CLAUDE_CLI = os.environ.get("CLAUDE_CLI")
if not CLAUDE_CLI:
    raise RuntimeError("CLAUDE_CLI environment variable must point to the claude CLI binary")
def refresh_via_cli(oauth):
    import subprocess
    old_expires = oauth.get("expiresAt", 0)
    old_oauth = oauth
    write_credentials({})
    env = {
        **os.environ,
        "CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_REFRESH_TOKEN": oauth["refreshToken"],
        "CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_SCOPES": " ".join(oauth.get("scopes", [])),
    }
    try:
        result = subprocess.run(
            [CLAUDE_CLI, "auth", "login"],
            env=env, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=30,
        )
        if result.returncode != 0:
            raise RuntimeError(f"claude auth login failed: stdout={result.stdout} stderr={result.stderr}")
        new_oauth = read_credentials()
        if not new_oauth or new_oauth.get("expiresAt", 0) <= old_expires:
            raise RuntimeError("claude auth login succeeded but credentials did not update")
        app.logger.info("Token refreshed via claude auth login (new expiry: %s)", new_oauth["expiresAt"])
    except Exception:
        write_credentials(old_oauth)
        raise
NTFY_URL = "http://192.168.1.46:9705/n"


def ntfy(message, priority="default"):
    try:
        http_requests.post(NTFY_URL, data=message.encode(),
                           headers={"Priority": priority, "Title": "remoteclaude"}, timeout=5)
    except Exception:
        app.logger.warning(f"Failed to send ntfy: {message}")
AUTH_ERROR_MARKERS = [
    "does not have access",
    "login again",
    "unauthorized",
    "authentication",
]


def is_auth_error(error_str):
    lower = error_str.lower()
    return any(marker in lower for marker in AUTH_ERROR_MARKERS)


def force_refresh_token():
    oauth = read_credentials()
    if not oauth or "refreshToken" not in oauth:
        raise RuntimeError("No refresh token available — re-authenticate manually")
    app.logger.info("Forcing token refresh via CLI...")
    refresh_via_cli(oauth)


def ensure_valid_token():
    oauth = read_credentials()
    if not oauth or "expiresAt" not in oauth:
        return
    now_ms = int(time.time() * 1000)
    margin_ms = 5 * 60 * 1000
    if now_ms < oauth["expiresAt"] - margin_ms:
        return
    app.logger.info("OAuth token expired or expiring soon, refreshing via CLI...")
    try:
        refresh_via_cli(oauth)
    except Exception as e:
        ntfy(f"Token refresh failed: {e}\nUpdate creds in Vault!", priority="high")
        raise
local_oauth = read_credentials()
if local_oauth and "expiresAt" in local_oauth:
    now_ms = int(time.time() * 1000)
    margin_ms = 5 * 60 * 1000
    if now_ms < local_oauth["expiresAt"] - margin_ms:
        app.logger.info("Using existing local credentials (still valid)")
    else:
        app.logger.info("Local credentials expired, falling back to Vault")
        local_oauth = None

if not local_oauth and ROLE_ID and SECRET_ID:
    if not load_credentials_from_vault():
        ntfy("No credentials found in Vault for remoteclaude!", priority="high")

try:
    ensure_valid_token()
except Exception as e:
    print(f"ERROR: Token invalid at startup: {e}", flush=True)
    sys.exit(1)
app_tokens: dict[str, float] = {}


@app.before_request
async def check_app_token():
    if request.path.startswith("/api/") and not request.path.startswith("/api/debug/"):
        token = request.headers.get("X-App-Token")
        now = time.time()
        if not token or token not in app_tokens or app_tokens[token] < now:
            app_tokens.pop(token, None)
            return jsonify({"error": "forbidden"}), 403

_SESSION_ID_RE = re.compile(r'^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,128}$')


def valid_session_id(sid):
    return bool(sid and _SESSION_ID_RE.match(sid))
_chat_semaphore = asyncio.Semaphore(1)
_chat_last_request = 0.0


def check_chat_rate_limit():
    global _chat_last_request
    now = time.time()
    if now - _chat_last_request < 2.0:
        print(f"    [rate] cooldown ({now - _chat_last_request:.1f}s since last)", flush=True)
        return jsonify({"error": "too many requests"}), 429
    if _chat_semaphore.locked():
        print("    [rate] semaphore locked", flush=True)
        return jsonify({"error": "query already in progress"}), 429
    _chat_last_request = now
    return None
_debug_enabled = os.environ.get("DEBUG", "1").lower() in ("1", "true")
_test_state = "idle"
_test_barrier_state = None
_test_barrier_event = None  # created lazily in the server's event loop


def _get_barrier_event():
    global _test_barrier_event
    if _test_barrier_event is None:
        _test_barrier_event = asyncio.Event()
        _test_barrier_event.set()
    return _test_barrier_event


async def set_test_state(state):
    global _test_state
    if not _debug_enabled:
        return
    _test_state = state
    evt = _get_barrier_event()
    if _test_barrier_state == state:
        evt.clear()
        await evt.wait()


if _debug_enabled:
    @app.route("/api/debug/state")
    async def debug_state():
        return jsonify({"state": _test_state})

    @app.route("/api/debug/barrier", methods=["POST"])
    async def debug_barrier():
        global _test_barrier_state
        data = await request.get_json()
        _test_barrier_state = data.get("state")
        _get_barrier_event().set()
        return jsonify({"ok": True, "barrier": _test_barrier_state})

    @app.route("/api/debug/resume", methods=["POST"])
    async def debug_resume():
        global _test_barrier_state
        _test_barrier_state = None
        _get_barrier_event().set()
        return jsonify({"ok": True})

App setup

The SDK is fully async, so we need an async web framework. Quart (async Flask) lets us await the SDK directly in request handlers without threading hacks.

The CLAUDECODE environment variable tells Claude Code it’s running inside another Claude Code session. When the app is launched from a terminal that happens to be a Claude Code session, this variable leaks through and confuses the subprocess. Removing it ensures the SDK always starts a fresh instance.

import asyncio
import json
import os
import re
import secrets
import sys
import time
import uuid

import requests as http_requests
from quart import Quart, Response, render_template, request, jsonify
from claude_agent_sdk import query, list_sessions, get_session_messages, ClaudeAgentOptions
from claude_agent_sdk.types import (
    StreamEvent, AssistantMessage, ResultMessage, TextBlock,
)

os.environ.pop("CLAUDECODE", None)

_current_query_task = None

app = Quart(__name__)

Where credentials live

To talk to Claude, the app needs an OAuth access token. That token lives on disk at ~/.claude/.credentials.json — the same location the Claude CLI uses, so both tools share the same credential seamlessly.

The disk copy serves as a cache: it avoids hitting Vault on every request and, critically, survives container restarts thanks to Nomad’s sticky ephemeral disk. A recently refreshed token from a previous allocation may still be valid, saving a Vault round-trip at startup.

CREDENTIALS_PATH = os.path.join(os.path.expanduser("~/.claude"), ".credentials.json")


def write_credentials(oauth):
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(CREDENTIALS_PATH), exist_ok=True)
    with open(CREDENTIALS_PATH, "w") as f:
        json.dump({"claudeAiOauth": oauth}, f)


def read_credentials():
    try:
        with open(CREDENTIALS_PATH) as f:
            return json.load(f).get("claudeAiOauth")
    except (FileNotFoundError, json.JSONDecodeError):
        return None

Fetching credentials from Vault

When the disk cache is empty (first deploy, or the ephemeral disk was recycled), the app falls back to Vault. The OAuth credentials are stored in Vault KV v2 so they never need to be baked into the container image or passed as plain-text environment variables. The app authenticates to Vault using AppRole — role ID and secret ID are injected by Nomad.

The Vault token has a 1 h TTL. Before each read, vault_renew extends it; if the token has already expired (403), it falls back to a fresh AppRole login. This means the app can sit idle for hours between Vault reads without losing access.

Vault stores all values as strings, so load_credentials_from_vault coerces types on the way out: expiresAt becomes an int, scopes is parsed from a JSON string back to a list.

VAULT_ADDR = os.environ.get("VAULT_ADDR", "http://127.0.0.1:8200")
ROLE_ID = os.environ.get("ROLE_ID")
SECRET_ID = os.environ.get("SECRET_ID")

_vault_token = None


def vault_login():
    global _vault_token
    r = http_requests.post(
        f"{VAULT_ADDR}/v1/auth/approle/login",
        json={"role_id": ROLE_ID, "secret_id": SECRET_ID},
    )
    r.raise_for_status()
    _vault_token = r.json()["auth"]["client_token"]


def vault_headers():
    return {"X-Vault-Token": _vault_token}


def vault_renew():
    r = http_requests.post(
        f"{VAULT_ADDR}/v1/auth/token/renew-self",
        headers=vault_headers(),
        json={"increment": "1h"},
    )
    if r.status_code == 403:
        vault_login()


def vault_read(key):
    vault_renew()
    r = http_requests.get(
        f"{VAULT_ADDR}/v1/secret/data/remoteclaude/{key}",
        headers=vault_headers(),
    )
    if r.status_code == 200:
        return r.json()["data"]["data"]
    return None


def load_credentials_from_vault():
    vault_login()
    creds = vault_read("creds")
    if not creds:
        return False
    oauth = dict(creds)
    if "expiresAt" in oauth:
        oauth["expiresAt"] = int(oauth["expiresAt"])
    if isinstance(oauth.get("scopes"), str):
        oauth["scopes"] = json.loads(oauth["scopes"])
    write_credentials(oauth)
    return True

Keeping the token fresh

The OAuth access token has a limited TTL (typically 1 h). When it expires, we need to exchange the refresh token for a new access token. The Claude CLI’s auth login command handles this flow internally. The CLI must be the Node.js version (@anthropic-ai/claude-code npm package), not the bundled binary from the SDK wheel — the bundled binary doesn’t support --permission-prompt-tool stdio properly. The Earthly build puts claude on PATH via npm install; the nix flake wraps node cli.js similarly.

CLAUDE_CLI = os.environ.get("CLAUDE_CLI")
if not CLAUDE_CLI:
    raise RuntimeError("CLAUDE_CLI environment variable must point to the claude CLI binary")

The refresh dance

Refreshing sounds simple — call claude auth login with the refresh token — but there is a subtlety. The CLI reads ~/.claude/.credentials.json on startup. If the file contains an expired access token, the CLI tries to use it and fails instead of picking up the refresh token from the environment. To work around this, we clear the credentials file before invoking the CLI, then restore the old credentials if the refresh fails. This ensures we never lose the refresh token even if the CLI crashes.

After the CLI returns successfully, we verify the credentials actually changed (the new expiresAt must be later than the old one). This catches edge cases where the CLI exits 0 but doesn’t actually write new credentials.

def refresh_via_cli(oauth):
    import subprocess
    old_expires = oauth.get("expiresAt", 0)
    old_oauth = oauth
    write_credentials({})
    env = {
        **os.environ,
        "CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_REFRESH_TOKEN": oauth["refreshToken"],
        "CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_SCOPES": " ".join(oauth.get("scopes", [])),
    }
    try:
        result = subprocess.run(
            [CLAUDE_CLI, "auth", "login"],
            env=env, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=30,
        )
        if result.returncode != 0:
            raise RuntimeError(f"claude auth login failed: stdout={result.stdout} stderr={result.stderr}")
        new_oauth = read_credentials()
        if not new_oauth or new_oauth.get("expiresAt", 0) <= old_expires:
            raise RuntimeError("claude auth login succeeded but credentials did not update")
        app.logger.info("Token refreshed via claude auth login (new expiry: %s)", new_oauth["expiresAt"])
    except Exception:
        write_credentials(old_oauth)
        raise

When things go wrong

The app runs unattended on a headless server. Authentication is the one thing that can’t self-heal indefinitely — eventually a refresh token expires or gets revoked, and a human needs to re-authenticate. When that happens, the app pushes a notification to the local ntfy instance so the operator knows to intervene. Failures to send the notification itself are logged but never raised — alerting should not make an already-bad situation worse.

NTFY_URL = "http://192.168.1.46:9705/n"


def ntfy(message, priority="default"):
    try:
        http_requests.post(NTFY_URL, data=message.encode(),
                           headers={"Priority": priority, "Title": "remoteclaude"}, timeout=5)
    except Exception:
        app.logger.warning(f"Failed to send ntfy: {message}")

Detecting and recovering from auth errors

Claude’s API returns various error messages when authentication fails. We match against a set of known markers to distinguish auth errors (which we can fix by refreshing the token) from other errors (which we should surface to the user). The matching is intentionally broad — a false positive just triggers an unnecessary token refresh, while a false negative shows the user a confusing auth error instead of recovering automatically.

ensure_valid_token is the main entry point, called before each query. It checks the local expiresAt timestamp with a 5-minute margin and refreshes proactively. force_refresh_token skips the timestamp check entirely — it’s used when the API returns an auth error despite the token appearing valid (clock skew, revocation). Both paths alert via ntfy if the refresh fails.

AUTH_ERROR_MARKERS = [
    "does not have access",
    "login again",
    "unauthorized",
    "authentication",
]


def is_auth_error(error_str):
    lower = error_str.lower()
    return any(marker in lower for marker in AUTH_ERROR_MARKERS)


def force_refresh_token():
    oauth = read_credentials()
    if not oauth or "refreshToken" not in oauth:
        raise RuntimeError("No refresh token available — re-authenticate manually")
    app.logger.info("Forcing token refresh via CLI...")
    refresh_via_cli(oauth)


def ensure_valid_token():
    oauth = read_credentials()
    if not oauth or "expiresAt" not in oauth:
        return
    now_ms = int(time.time() * 1000)
    margin_ms = 5 * 60 * 1000
    if now_ms < oauth["expiresAt"] - margin_ms:
        return
    app.logger.info("OAuth token expired or expiring soon, refreshing via CLI...")
    try:
        refresh_via_cli(oauth)
    except Exception as e:
        ntfy(f"Token refresh failed: {e}\nUpdate creds in Vault!", priority="high")
        raise

Startup: putting it all together

At startup, the app walks the credential chain: try the disk cache first (fast, works if the sticky disk has a recent token), fall back to Vault if the cache is missing or stale, then verify we ended up with something usable. If not, the app exits immediately — there’s no point starting a web server that can’t talk to Claude.

local_oauth = read_credentials()
if local_oauth and "expiresAt" in local_oauth:
    now_ms = int(time.time() * 1000)
    margin_ms = 5 * 60 * 1000
    if now_ms < local_oauth["expiresAt"] - margin_ms:
        app.logger.info("Using existing local credentials (still valid)")
    else:
        app.logger.info("Local credentials expired, falling back to Vault")
        local_oauth = None

if not local_oauth and ROLE_ID and SECRET_ID:
    if not load_credentials_from_vault():
        ntfy("No credentials found in Vault for remoteclaude!", priority="high")

try:
    ensure_valid_token()
except Exception as e:
    print(f"ERROR: Token invalid at startup: {e}", flush=True)
    sys.exit(1)

Guarding API requests

With authentication sorted, we can now protect the runtime. The app is exposed to the network behind Traefik’s ForwardAuth, but defense-in-depth means we don’t trust that alone. Each page load mints a fresh secrets.token_urlsafe(32) (valid 24 h) that gets embedded in the HTML via a <meta> tag. Every /api/ request must include this token in an X-App-Token header.

This per-page-load token design has nice properties. It blocks CSRF: a cross-origin page cannot read the meta tag, so it cannot construct the header. If Traefik is bypassed (misconfiguration, direct port access), API endpoints are still protected — an attacker who reaches the server can load the page but the token they get only works for that tab. A leaked token compromises one browser session, not every user. And because the root page is excluded from the service worker’s PRECACHE list, tokens are always fetched fresh from the server — a cached page never carries a stale token.

Session IDs come from the SDK and are opaque strings. We validate them against a strict regex before passing them to any SDK function to prevent path traversal or injection through crafted IDs.

app_tokens: dict[str, float] = {}


@app.before_request
async def check_app_token():
    if request.path.startswith("/api/") and not request.path.startswith("/api/debug/"):
        token = request.headers.get("X-App-Token")
        now = time.time()
        if not token or token not in app_tokens or app_tokens[token] < now:
            app_tokens.pop(token, None)
            return jsonify({"error": "forbidden"}), 403

_SESSION_ID_RE = re.compile(r'^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,128}$')


def valid_session_id(sid):
    return bool(sid and _SESSION_ID_RE.match(sid))
App token required for API

API endpoints should reject requests without a valid X-App-Token header.

def test_token_required_for_api(page):
    """API returns 403 without a valid app token."""
    import requests as http_requests
    fresh_page(page)
    base = page.url.rstrip("/")
    # No token
    r = http_requests.get(f"{base}/api/sessions")
    assert r.status_code == 403, f"Expected 403 without token, got {r.status_code}"
    # Bad token
    r = http_requests.get(f"{base}/api/sessions", headers={"X-App-Token": "bogus"})
    assert r.status_code == 403, f"Expected 403 with bad token, got {r.status_code}"
    print("  PASS: app token required for API")

Rate limiting

Each /api/chat request spawns a Claude Code process, which is expensive in CPU, memory, and API quota. Without limits, an accidental client loop or a curious attacker could exhaust the server. Since this is a single-user app, the simplest effective defense is a concurrency limit: only one query at a time. A second request while one is in flight gets a 429.

On top of that, a minimum 2-second cooldown between requests prevents rapid fire even after the previous one finishes. Together these ensure the server never runs more than one Claude process and can’t be hammered faster than once every 2 seconds.

_chat_semaphore = asyncio.Semaphore(1)
_chat_last_request = 0.0


def check_chat_rate_limit():
    global _chat_last_request
    now = time.time()
    if now - _chat_last_request < 2.0:
        print(f"    [rate] cooldown ({now - _chat_last_request:.1f}s since last)", flush=True)
        return jsonify({"error": "too many requests"}), 429
    if _chat_semaphore.locked():
        print("    [rate] semaphore locked", flush=True)
        return jsonify({"error": "query already in progress"}), 429
    _chat_last_request = now
    return None
Rate limiting

Two rapid requests to /api/chat should get a 429 on the second one (2-second cooldown). Also verify that a request while a query is in progress gets 429 (concurrency limit).

def test_rate_limiting(page):
    """Concurrent chat requests get 429."""
    import requests as http_requests
    fresh_page(page)
    base = page.url.rstrip("/")
    token = page.locator("meta[name=app-token]").get_attribute("content")
    headers = {"X-App-Token": token, "Content-Type": "application/json"}
    body = {"prompt": "Say only 'ok'"}
    # Send r1 streaming, then immediately send r2 while r1 is in progress
    r1 = http_requests.post(f"{base}/api/chat", headers=headers, json=body, stream=True)
    assert r1.status_code == 200, f"First request should succeed, got {r1.status_code}"
    # r1 is still streaming — second request hits concurrency limit
    r2 = http_requests.post(f"{base}/api/chat", headers=headers, json=body)
    assert r2.status_code == 429, f"Expected 429 for concurrent request, got {r2.status_code}"
    # Consume r1 fully so server-side query finishes and releases semaphore
    for _ in r1.iter_content():
        pass
    r1.close()
    print("  PASS: rate limiting")

Debug barriers for deterministic testing

The app’s state transitions (idle → streaming → done) can outrun the test suite, especially in mock mode where SDK calls replay instantly. Rather than sprinkling sleeps, we add a synchronization mechanism: the app tracks its state and can be told to pause at specific states, letting the test catch up before resuming.

The barrier system is gated by DEBUG — in production (DEBUG=0) the state setter is a no-op and the debug endpoints are not registered at all.

_debug_enabled = os.environ.get("DEBUG", "1").lower() in ("1", "true")
_test_state = "idle"
_test_barrier_state = None
_test_barrier_event = None  # created lazily in the server's event loop


def _get_barrier_event():
    global _test_barrier_event
    if _test_barrier_event is None:
        _test_barrier_event = asyncio.Event()
        _test_barrier_event.set()
    return _test_barrier_event


async def set_test_state(state):
    global _test_state
    if not _debug_enabled:
        return
    _test_state = state
    evt = _get_barrier_event()
    if _test_barrier_state == state:
        evt.clear()
        await evt.wait()


if _debug_enabled:
    @app.route("/api/debug/state")
    async def debug_state():
        return jsonify({"state": _test_state})

    @app.route("/api/debug/barrier", methods=["POST"])
    async def debug_barrier():
        global _test_barrier_state
        data = await request.get_json()
        _test_barrier_state = data.get("state")
        _get_barrier_event().set()
        return jsonify({"ok": True, "barrier": _test_barrier_state})

    @app.route("/api/debug/resume", methods=["POST"])
    async def debug_resume():
        global _test_barrier_state
        _test_barrier_state = None
        _get_barrier_event().set()
        return jsonify({"ok": True})

Background token refresh

The OAuth token has a limited TTL, but the app may sit idle for hours between conversations. Without proactive renewal the token would silently expire, and the next user message would fail. A background asyncio task solves this: it sleeps until 10 minutes before expiry, then refreshes. If the credentials lack an expiration date, something is wrong — we alert via ntfy and stop rather than polling blindly.

async def _token_refresh_loop():
    while True:
        oauth = read_credentials()
        if not (oauth and "expiresAt" in oauth):
            ntfy("No expiresAt in credentials — cannot schedule token refresh!", priority="high")
            return
        now_ms = int(time.time() * 1000)
        margin_ms = 10 * 60 * 1000  # refresh 10 min before expiry
        delay_s = max(60, (oauth["expiresAt"] - now_ms - margin_ms) / 1000)
        app.logger.debug("Background token refresh: sleeping %.0fs", delay_s)
        await asyncio.sleep(delay_s)
        try:
            ensure_valid_token()
            app.logger.debug("Background token refresh: OK")
        except Exception as e:
            app.logger.warning("Background token refresh failed: %s", e)


@app.before_serving
async def start_background_refresh():
    asyncio.create_task(_token_refresh_loop())

Browsing past conversations

Claude Code sessions persist on disk. Being able to revisit past conversations is important — you might start a task on your phone, then continue it later, or want to check what Claude did yesterday.

The sidebar lists recent sessions; clicking one loads the full history. The communication between frontend and backend is straightforward REST:

  • GET /api/sessions → JSON array of {session_id, summary, first_prompt, …}
  • GET /api/sessions/<id>/messages → JSON array of structured messages

The sidebar

On mobile, screen space is precious. The sidebar becomes a slide-in drawer with a semi-transparent overlay — tapping outside it closes the drawer and returns focus to the conversation. Session titles don’t wrap: the list scrolls both vertically and horizontally so you can swipe to read long names.

The sidebar template iterates over sessions (populated by loadSessions at page load). Clicking an entry calls selectSession(s), which GETs /api/sessions/<id>/messages and populates the messages array. newChat() clears the session to start fresh.

<!-- Overlay (mobile) -->
<div x-show="sidebarOpen" x-transition.opacity
     @click="sidebarOpen = false"
     class="fixed inset-0 bg-black/50 z-40 md:hidden"></div>

<!-- Sidebar -->
<div :class="sidebarOpen ? 'translate-x-0' : '-translate-x-full'"
     class="fixed md:static md:translate-x-0 z-50 w-64 h-full bg-dark-sidebar border-r border-dark-accent p-4 flex flex-col overflow-hidden transition-transform duration-200">
  <button @click="newChat()" class="bg-dark-accent hover:bg-dark-hover text-gray-200 rounded-md py-2 px-3 text-sm mb-4 shrink-0">+ New Chat</button>
  <h2 class="text-xs text-gray-500 mb-2 uppercase tracking-wide shrink-0">Sessions</h2>
  <div class="overflow-x-auto overflow-y-auto no-scrollbar pan-xy flex-1">
    <div class="w-max min-w-full">
      <template x-for="s in sessions" :key="s.session_id">
        <div @click="selectSession(s)"
             :class="s.session_id === sessionId ? 'bg-dark-accent' : ''"
             class="py-2 px-3 rounded-md cursor-pointer hover:bg-dark-accent mb-1">
          <div class="text-lg font-medium text-white whitespace-nowrap" x-text="s.first_prompt || s.summary || s.session_id.slice(0, 12)"></div>
          <div class="text-[0.65rem] text-gray-500" x-text="relativeTime(s.last_modified)"></div>
        </div>
      </template>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>

Here are the handlers that power the sidebar. loadSessions fetches the list; selectSession loads a full conversation by GETting structured messages and pushing them into the messages array (which the templates in Sending messages render).

async loadSessions() {
  try {
    const resp = await fetch('api/sessions', { headers: authHeaders });
    this.sessions = await resp.json();
  } catch (e) {}
},

newChat() {
  this.sessionId = null;
  this.sessionCwd = null;
  this.messages = [];
  this.sidebarOpen = false;
},

async selectSession(s) {
  this.sessionId = s.session_id;
  this.sessionCwd = s.cwd || null;
  this.messages = [];
  this.sidebarOpen = false;
  try {
    const resp = await fetch(`api/sessions/${s.session_id}/messages`, { headers: authHeaders });
    const history = await resp.json();
    for (const m of history) {
      if (m.role === 'user') {
        this.messages.push({ type: 'user', content: m.content });
      } else {
        this.messages.push({ type: 'assistant', blocks: m.blocks || [{ type: 'text', content: m.content || '' }] });
      }
    }
    this.$nextTick(() => this.scrollToBottom());
  } catch (e) {}
},

scrollToBottom() {
  const el = this.$refs.messages;
  if (el) el.scrollTop = el.scrollHeight;
},

Sessions API

On the backend, these handlers wrap two SDK calls. list_sessions returns recent sessions (the sidebar data). get_session_messages returns the full conversation, but needs filtering: the SDK stores internal XML tags (system reminders, command outputs) alongside real user prompts, and we skip those so the history reads cleanly. Assistant messages come as structured blocks (text, thinking, tool calls) so the frontend can render them with appropriate folding.

@app.route("/api/sessions")
async def sessions():
    items = list_sessions(limit=20)
    return jsonify([
        {
            "session_id": s.session_id,
            "summary": s.summary,
            "last_modified": s.last_modified,
            "first_prompt": s.first_prompt,
            "cwd": getattr(s, "cwd", None),
        }
        for s in items
    ])


@app.route("/api/sessions/<session_id>/messages")
async def session_messages(session_id):
    if not valid_session_id(session_id):
        return jsonify({"error": "invalid session_id"}), 400
    msgs = get_session_messages(session_id)
    result = []
    for m in msgs:
        if m.type not in ("user", "assistant"):
            continue
        msg = m.message
        content = msg.get("content", "")

        if m.type == "user":
            if isinstance(content, list):
                text = ""
                for block in content:
                    if isinstance(block, dict) and block.get("type") == "text":
                        text += block.get("text", "")
                content = text
            stripped = content.strip() if isinstance(content, str) else ""
            if not stripped or stripped.startswith("<"):
                continue
            result.append({"role": "user", "content": content})
        else:
            blocks = []
            if isinstance(content, list):
                for block in content:
                    if not isinstance(block, dict):
                        continue
                    bt = block.get("type")
                    if bt == "text":
                        text = block.get("text", "").strip()
                        if text:
                            blocks.append({"type": "text", "content": text})
                    elif bt == "thinking":
                        text = block.get("thinking", "").strip()
                        if text:
                            blocks.append({"type": "thinking", "content": text})
                    elif bt == "tool_use":
                        blocks.append({
                            "type": "tool_use",
                            "name": block.get("name", ""),
                            "input": block.get("input", {}),
                        })
            if blocks:
                result.append({"role": "assistant", "blocks": blocks})
    return jsonify(result)

def test_invalid_session_id_rejected(page):
    """Session IDs with special chars are rejected."""
    import requests as http_requests
    fresh_page(page)
    base = page.url.rstrip("/")
    token = page.locator("meta[name=app-token]").get_attribute("content")
    headers = {"X-App-Token": token}
    for bad_id in ["foo+bar", "a" * 200, "sess;DROP", "sess.evil"]:
        r = http_requests.get(f"{base}/api/sessions/{bad_id}/messages", headers=headers)
        assert r.status_code == 400, f"Expected 400 for '{bad_id}', got {r.status_code}"
    # Valid ID should not 400 (may 200 with empty list)
    r = http_requests.get(f"{base}/api/sessions/valid-session-123/messages", headers=headers)
    assert r.status_code == 200, f"Expected 200 for valid ID, got {r.status_code}"
    print("  PASS: invalid session ID rejected")

Session resume passes cwd

When the user opens a past session and sends a message, the app resumes it via the SDK. The CLI needs the session’s original working directory to find the session files — without it, claude --resume fails with “No conversation found”. The frontend sends the session’s cwd alongside session_id, and the backend passes it as options.cwd.

    page.locator("div.cursor-pointer").first.click()
    page.wait_for_selector("text=You", timeout=TIMEOUT)

Sending messages

The main interaction: the user types a message (optionally attaches images) and Claude responds. The communication uses Server-Sent Events (SSE) so tokens stream to the browser as they arrive rather than waiting for the full response.

The flow crosses the client-server boundary three times:

  1. The browser POST​s to /api/chat with {prompt, session_id, images}
  2. The server returns an SSE stream with text, error, and done events
  3. When the stream ends, the done event carries the session ID for future resumption

Message display

The conversation view renders three kinds of messages: user, assistant, and error. Claude’s responses are rich — they contain text, internal thinking, and tool calls. Regular text appears inline; thinking and tool calls are collapsed inside <details> elements to avoid overwhelming the reader. During streaming (before structured blocks arrive), raw text is shown directly.

                        <div class="px-3 pb-2 text-xs text-gray-500 whitespace-pre-wrap" x-text="block.content"></div>

Message input

On a phone, the input area is the main interaction point. The textarea auto-grows as you type (no tiny fixed box) and Enter sends immediately (the @keydown.enter handler calls sendMessage()). Shift+Enter adds a newline for multi-line prompts. The camera button opens a file picker (@click → $refs.fileInput.click()), and handlePaste intercepts clipboard paste events to capture images. Both feed into addFiles, which converts images to base64 and pushes them into pendingImages — shown as thumbnails above the input.

The Send button swaps to a red Cancel button while a query is in flight (x-show toggles on sending). Tapping Cancel fires cancelQuery(), which POSTs to /api/cancel and aborts the running SDK task. The button returns to Send once the stream ends. x-cloak on the Cancel button prevents a flash of red before Alpine initialises.

    <!-- Image previews -->
    <template x-if="pendingImages.length">
      <div class="flex gap-2 px-4 pt-2 border-t border-dark-accent bg-dark-sidebar overflow-x-auto">

</div>

sendMessage has three phases, each explained below. fileToBase64 and addFiles convert attached images to base64 before sending.

fileToBase64(file) {
  return new Promise((resolve) => {
    const reader = new FileReader();
    reader.onload = () => {
      const b64 = reader.result.split(',')[1];
      resolve({ media_type: file.type || 'image/png', data: b64 });
    };
    reader.readAsDataURL(file);
  });
},

async addFiles(files) {
  for (const f of files) {
    if (f.type.startsWith('image/')) {
      this.pendingImages.push(await this.fileToBase64(f));
    }
  }
},

async sendMessage() {
  const text = this.prompt.trim();
  const images = this.pendingImages.slice();
  this.prompt = '';
  this.pendingImages = [];
  this.sending = true;

  this.messages.push({ type: 'user', content: text, images: images.length ? images : null });
  const assistantMsg = { type: 'assistant', content: '', loading: true, elapsed: 0 };
  this.messages.push(assistantMsg);
  const msgIdx = this.messages.length - 1;

  const timer = setInterval(() => { assistantMsg.elapsed++; }, 1000);
  try {
    const resp = await fetch('api/chat', {
      method: 'POST',
      headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json', ...authHeaders },
      body: JSON.stringify({ prompt: text, session_id: this.sessionId, cwd: this.sessionCwd, images: images.length ? images : undefined }),
    });

    if (!resp.ok) {
      throw new Error(`HTTP ${resp.status}: ${resp.statusText}`);
    }

    const reader = resp.body.getReader();
    const decoder = new TextDecoder();
    let buffer = '';

    while (true) {
      const { done, value } = await reader.read();
      if (done) break;
      buffer += decoder.decode(value, { stream: true });

      const lines = buffer.split('\n');
      buffer = lines.pop();

      let eventType = null;
      for (const line of lines) {
        if (line.startsWith('event: ')) {
          eventType = line.slice(7);
        } else if (line.startsWith('data: ') && eventType) {
          const data = JSON.parse(line.slice(6));
          if (eventType === 'text') {
            this.messages[msgIdx].content += data;
          } else if (eventType === 'error') {
            this.messages.push({ type: 'error', content: data });
          } else if (eventType === 'cancelled') {
            this.messages[msgIdx].content += '\n\n*[Cancelled]*';
          } else if (eventType === 'done') {
            this.sessionId = data;
            this.loadSessions();
          }
          eventType = null;
        }
      }
    }
  } catch (err) {
    this.messages.push({ type: 'error', content: err.message });
  }
  clearInterval(timer);
  this.messages[msgIdx].loading = false;
  this.sending = false;
},

Consuming the SSE stream

POST to /api/chat and read the response as a stream of SSE frames. Each frame has an event: line and a data: line. The event type determines what happens:

  • text → append to the assistant message (character by character streaming)
  • error → show an error card
  • cancelled → append a “[Cancelled]” marker to the assistant message
  • done → store the session ID for resumption, refresh the sidebar

try {
  const resp = await fetch('api/chat', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json', ...authHeaders },
    body: JSON.stringify({ prompt: text, session_id: this.sessionId, cwd: this.sessionCwd, images: images.length ? images : undefined }),
  });

  if (!resp.ok) {
    throw new Error(`HTTP ${resp.status}: ${resp.statusText}`);
  }

  const reader = resp.body.getReader();
  const decoder = new TextDecoder();
  let buffer = '';

  while (true) {
    const { done, value } = await reader.read();
    if (done) break;
    buffer += decoder.decode(value, { stream: true });

    const lines = buffer.split('\n');
    buffer = lines.pop();

    let eventType = null;
    for (const line of lines) {
      if (line.startsWith('event: ')) {
        eventType = line.slice(7);
      } else if (line.startsWith('data: ') && eventType) {
        const data = JSON.parse(line.slice(6));
        if (eventType === 'text') {
          this.messages[msgIdx].content += data;
        } else if (eventType === 'error') {
          this.messages.push({ type: 'error', content: data });
        } else if (eventType === 'cancelled') {
          this.messages[msgIdx].content += '\n\n*[Cancelled]*';
        } else if (eventType === 'done') {
          this.sessionId = data;
          this.loadSessions();
        }
        eventType = null;
      }
    }
  }
} catch (err) {
  this.messages.push({ type: 'error', content: err.message });
}

The chat endpoint

The browser’s entry point. It validates the input and returns the SSE stream from generate_sse. The X-Accel-Buffering: no header tells nginx (or any reverse proxy) not to buffer the stream — without it, tokens would batch up and arrive in bursts instead of flowing smoothly.

@app.route("/api/chat", methods=["POST"])
async def chat():
    body = await request.get_json()
    prompt = body.get("prompt", "")
    session_id = body.get("session_id")
    cwd = body.get("cwd")
    images = body.get("images")
    print(f"    [chat] POST /api/chat prompt={prompt[:50]!r} session={session_id}", flush=True)
    if session_id and not valid_session_id(session_id):
        return jsonify({"error": "invalid session_id"}), 400
    if not prompt and not images:
        return jsonify({"error": "prompt or images required"}), 400
    rate_err = check_chat_rate_limit()
    if rate_err:
        return rate_err
    return Response(
        generate_sse(prompt, session_id, cwd=cwd, images=images),
        mimetype="text/event-stream",
        headers={"Cache-Control": "no-cache", "X-Accel-Buffering": "no"},
    )

Chat rejects empty request

The chat endpoint should reject requests with neither prompt nor images.

def test_chat_rejects_empty_request(page):
    """Chat endpoint returns 400 for empty prompt and no images."""
    import requests as http_requests
    fresh_page(page)
    base = page.url.rstrip("/")
    token = page.locator("meta[name=app-token]").get_attribute("content")
    headers = {"X-App-Token": token, "Content-Type": "application/json"}
    r = http_requests.post(f"{base}/api/chat", headers=headers, json={"prompt": "", "images": None})
    assert r.status_code == 400, f"Expected 400, got {r.status_code}"
    r = http_requests.post(f"{base}/api/chat", headers=headers, json={})
    assert r.status_code == 400, f"Expected 400 for empty body, got {r.status_code}"
    print("  PASS: chat rejects empty request")

The SSE pipeline

generate_sse is the heart of the streaming pipeline on the server side — it mirrors what sendMessage consumes on the client side. The architecture: the SDK query runs as an asyncio task that pushes events (text, errors, done) into an asyncio.Queue. An SSE async generator drains that queue and yields formatted events to the browser. This decouples production (SDK) from consumption (HTTP response).

async def generate_sse(prompt, session_id=None, cwd=None, images=None):
    """Run claude-agent-sdk query and yield SSE events."""
    global _current_query_task
    print(f"    [sse] waiting for semaphore (locked={_chat_semaphore.locked()})", flush=True)
    await _chat_semaphore.acquire()
    print(f"    [sse] acquired, prompt={prompt[:50]!r} session={session_id}", flush=True)
    try:
        ensure_valid_token()
        q = asyncio.Queue()

        def make_prompt():
            if images:
                content = []
                for img in images:
                    content.append({
                        "type": "image",
                        "source": {
                            "type": "base64",
                            "media_type": img["media_type"],
                            "data": img["data"],
                        },
                    })
                if prompt:
                    content.append({"type": "text", "text": prompt})
                return {"type": "user", "message": {"role": "user", "content": content}}
            return {"type": "user", "message": {"role": "user", "content": prompt}}
        async def collect():
            stderr_lines = []
            def on_stderr(line):
                stderr_lines.append(line)

            options = ClaudeAgentOptions(
                cli_path=CLAUDE_CLI,
                include_partial_messages=True,
                permission_mode='bypassPermissions',
                stderr=on_stderr,
                debug_stderr=on_stderr,
            )
            if session_id:
                options.resume = session_id
            if cwd:
                options.cwd = cwd

            prompt_msg = make_prompt()

            async def prompt_iter():
                yield prompt_msg

            result_session_id = session_id or ""
            try:
                async for message in query(prompt=prompt_iter(), options=options):
                    if isinstance(message, StreamEvent):
                        event = message.event
                        if event.get("type") == "content_block_delta":
                            delta = event.get("delta", {})
                            if delta.get("type") == "text_delta":
                                text = delta.get("text", "")
                                if text:
                                    await q.put(("text", text))
                    elif isinstance(message, ResultMessage):
                        result_session_id = message.session_id
            except Exception as e:
                detail = "\n".join(stderr_lines[-20:]) if stderr_lines else str(e)
                raise Exception(detail) from e
            await q.put(("done", result_session_id))
        async def collect_with_retry():
            try:
                await collect()
            except Exception as e:
                if is_auth_error(str(e)):
                    app.logger.warning("Auth error detected, forcing token refresh and retrying...")
                    try:
                        force_refresh_token()
                    except Exception as refresh_err:
                        ntfy(f"Auth error + refresh failed: {refresh_err}\nRe-authenticate manually!", priority="high")
                        raise e
                    await collect()
                else:
                    raise
        async def run_query():
            try:
                await set_test_state("streaming")
                await collect_with_retry()
            except asyncio.CancelledError:
                await q.put(("cancelled", "Query cancelled"))
            except Exception as e:
                import traceback
                traceback.print_exc()
                await q.put(("error", str(e)))
            finally:
                global _current_query_task
                _current_query_task = None
                await q.put(None)

        _current_query_task = asyncio.create_task(run_query())
        while True:
            item = await q.get()
            if item is None:
                break
            event_type, data = item
            yield f"event: {event_type}\ndata: {json.dumps(data)}\n\n"
    finally:
        await set_test_state("idle")
        _chat_semaphore.release()


@app.route("/api/chat", methods=["POST"])
async def chat():
    body = await request.get_json()
    prompt = body.get("prompt", "")
    session_id = body.get("session_id")
    cwd = body.get("cwd")
    images = body.get("images")
    print(f"    [chat] POST /api/chat prompt={prompt[:50]!r} session={session_id}", flush=True)
    if session_id and not valid_session_id(session_id):
        return jsonify({"error": "invalid session_id"}), 400
    if not prompt and not images:
        return jsonify({"error": "prompt or images required"}), 400
    rate_err = check_chat_rate_limit()
    if rate_err:
        return rate_err
    return Response(
        generate_sse(prompt, session_id, cwd=cwd, images=images),
        mimetype="text/event-stream",
        headers={"Cache-Control": "no-cache", "X-Accel-Buffering": "no"},
    )


@app.route("/api/cancel", methods=["POST"])
async def cancel_query():
    global _current_query_task
    if _current_query_task and not _current_query_task.done():
        _current_query_task.cancel()
        return jsonify({"ok": True})
    return jsonify({"error": "no query in progress"}), 404

Building the prompt message

The SDK expects a specific message format. Text-only prompts are simple strings, but when the user attaches images (photos from a phone camera, screenshots), we need to build a multipart content array with base64-encoded image blocks. This helper encapsulates that formatting so collect can focus on the query itself.

def make_prompt():
    if images:
        content = []
        for img in images:
            content.append({
                "type": "image",
                "source": {
                    "type": "base64",
                    "media_type": img["media_type"],
                    "data": img["data"],
                },
            })
        if prompt:
            content.append({"type": "text", "text": prompt})
        return {"type": "user", "message": {"role": "user", "content": content}}
    return {"type": "user", "message": {"role": "user", "content": prompt}}

Collecting streamed responses

This is where we actually talk to Claude. The SDK yields a stream of typed messages: StreamEvent for partial content (text deltas) and ResultMessage when the conversation is done (with a session ID for resumption). We forward text deltas into the queue so the browser sees them immediately. Stderr is captured separately — if the query crashes, the last 20 lines of stderr usually contain the real error, which is more useful than the generic exception message.

async def collect():
    stderr_lines = []
    def on_stderr(line):
        stderr_lines.append(line)

    options = ClaudeAgentOptions(
        cli_path=CLAUDE_CLI,
        include_partial_messages=True,
        permission_mode='bypassPermissions',
        stderr=on_stderr,
        debug_stderr=on_stderr,
    )
    if session_id:
        options.resume = session_id
    if cwd:
        options.cwd = cwd

    prompt_msg = make_prompt()

    async def prompt_iter():
        yield prompt_msg

    result_session_id = session_id or ""
    try:
        async for message in query(prompt=prompt_iter(), options=options):
            if isinstance(message, StreamEvent):
                event = message.event
                if event.get("type") == "content_block_delta":
                    delta = event.get("delta", {})
                    if delta.get("type") == "text_delta":
                        text = delta.get("text", "")
                        if text:
                            await q.put(("text", text))
            elif isinstance(message, ResultMessage):
                result_session_id = message.session_id
    except Exception as e:
        detail = "\n".join(stderr_lines[-20:]) if stderr_lines else str(e)
        raise Exception(detail) from e
    await q.put(("done", result_session_id))

Retry on auth errors

OAuth tokens can expire mid-conversation despite our background refresh (clock skew, Vault hiccups). Rather than showing the user a cryptic auth error, we detect it, force a token refresh, and retry the query once. If even the refresh fails, the situation needs human attention — we alert via ntfy so the operator knows to re-authenticate manually.

async def collect_with_retry():
    try:
        await collect()
    except Exception as e:
        if is_auth_error(str(e)):
            app.logger.warning("Auth error detected, forcing token refresh and retrying...")
            try:
                force_refresh_token()
            except Exception as refresh_err:
                ntfy(f"Auth error + refresh failed: {refresh_err}\nRe-authenticate manually!", priority="high")
                raise e
            await collect()
        else:
            raise

Running the query as a background task

The SSE generator is an async generator that the HTTP response consumes. It can’t both drive the SDK query and yield events — so we run the query in a separate asyncio task. The task pushes events into the queue; the generator yields them. When the task finishes (success or failure), it pushes None as a sentinel so the generator knows to stop. Errors are forwarded as ("error", msg) events rather than raised, because the HTTP response is already in flight.

The task reference is stored in _current_query_task so the cancel endpoint can abort it. When cancelled, CancelledError propagates up from whichever await the SDK is currently blocked on, and the task pushes a ("cancelled", ...) event before the sentinel — so the browser can show a “[Cancelled]” marker instead of leaving the response hanging.

async def run_query():
    try:
        await set_test_state("streaming")
        await collect_with_retry()
    except asyncio.CancelledError:
        await q.put(("cancelled", "Query cancelled"))
    except Exception as e:
        import traceback
        traceback.print_exc()
        await q.put(("error", str(e)))
    finally:
        global _current_query_task
        _current_query_task = None
        await q.put(None)

_current_query_task = asyncio.create_task(run_query())

SSE generator loop

The consumer side of the queue. Each item becomes one SSE frame (event: type\ndata: json\n\n). The None sentinel ends the stream, which tells the browser the response is complete.

while True:
    item = await q.get()
    if item is None:
        break
    event_type, data = item
    yield f"event: {event_type}\ndata: {json.dumps(data)}\n\n"

Send text message

Sending a message should display it in the chat and show the response.

def test_send_text_message(page):
    """Sending text shows user message and assistant response."""
    fresh_page(page)
    page.locator("textarea").fill("Say only the word 'pong'")
    page.locator("button:text('Send')").click()
    # User message present
    assert page.locator("text=You").first.is_visible()
    # Assistant message present
    page.wait_for_selector("text=Claude", timeout=TIMEOUT)
    assert page.locator("text=Claude").first.is_visible()
    print("  PASS: send text message")

Cancel

When the user taps Cancel, the browser fires a POST to /api/cancel. There is no response body to process — the cancellation surfaces through the SSE stream as a cancelled event (handled in Consuming the SSE stream), which the sendMessage loop picks up on its next iteration.

async cancelQuery() {
  await fetch('api/cancel', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: authHeaders,
  });
},

Cancel endpoint

When the user clicks Cancel, the browser POSTs to /api/cancel. This endpoint cancels the running asyncio task, which raises CancelledError inside run_query. The task catches it, pushes a cancelled event to the SSE queue, and the stream ends cleanly.

@app.route("/api/cancel", methods=["POST"])
async def cancel_query():
    global _current_query_task
    if _current_query_task and not _current_query_task.done():
        _current_query_task.cancel()
        return jsonify({"ok": True})
    return jsonify({"error": "no query in progress"}), 404

Cancel running query

Clicking Cancel while a query is in progress should abort it and show a cancelled message.

def test_cancel_query(page):
    """Cancel button aborts a running query."""
    fresh_page(page)
    base = page.url.rstrip("/")
    # Tell the app to pause once it enters "streaming" state
    set_barrier(base, "streaming")
    page.locator("textarea").fill("Write a very long essay about the history of computing")
    page.locator("button:text('Send')").click()
    # Wait until the app is paused in streaming state (deterministic)
    wait_for_state(base, "streaming")
    page.wait_for_selector("button:text('Cancel')", timeout=TIMEOUT)
    page.locator("button:text('Cancel')").click()
    # Resume the app so it can process the cancellation
    resume_app(base)
    # Should show cancelled message and return to Send state
    page.wait_for_selector("text=[Cancelled]", timeout=TIMEOUT)
    page.wait_for_selector("button:text('Send')", timeout=TIMEOUT)
    # Wait for app to return to idle so _current_query_task is cleaned up
    wait_for_state(base, "idle")
    print("  PASS: cancel query")

Cancel with no query running

The cancel endpoint should return 404 when no query is in progress.

def test_cancel_no_query(page):
    """Cancel endpoint returns 404 when no query is running."""
    import requests as http_requests
    fresh_page(page)
    base = page.url.rstrip("/")
    token = page.locator("meta[name=app-token]").get_attribute("content")
    headers = {"X-App-Token": token}
    r = http_requests.post(f"{base}/api/cancel", headers=headers)
    assert r.status_code == 404, f"Expected 404, got {r.status_code}"
    print("  PASS: cancel no query")

Alpine component assembly

All client-side state lives in a single Alpine component. The pieces are explained alongside their features above; this block assembles them into the <script> tag that closes the HTML template.

<script>
function relativeTime(dateStr) {
  if (!dateStr) return '';
  const d = new Date(dateStr), now = new Date();
  const diffS = Math.floor((now - d) / 1000);
  if (diffS < 60) return 'just now';
  const diffM = Math.floor(diffS / 60);
  if (diffM < 60) return diffM + 'm ago';
  const diffH = Math.floor(diffM / 60);
  if (diffH < 24) return diffH + 'h ago';
  const diffD = Math.floor(diffH / 24);
  if (diffD === 1) return 'yesterday';
  if (diffD < 7) return diffD + 'd ago';
  return d.toLocaleDateString(undefined, { month: 'short', day: 'numeric' });
}

marked.setOptions({ gfm: true, breaks: true });
const renderer = new marked.Renderer();
renderer.code = function({ text, lang }) {
  let highlighted;
  if (lang && hljs.getLanguage(lang)) {
    highlighted = hljs.highlight(text, { language: lang }).value;
  } else {
    highlighted = hljs.highlightAuto(text).value;
  }
  return '<pre><code class="hljs">' + highlighted + '</code></pre>';
};
marked.use({ renderer });
function renderMarkdown(text) {
  if (!text) return '';
  return marked.parse(text);
}

function chatApp() {
  const appToken = document.querySelector('meta[name=app-token]').content;
  const authHeaders = { 'X-App-Token': appToken };
  return {
    sessionId: null,
    sessionCwd: null,
    sessions: [],
    messages: [],
    prompt: '',
    sending: false,
    sidebarOpen: false,
    pendingImages: [],

    relativeTime: relativeTime,

async loadSessions() {
  try {
    const resp = await fetch('api/sessions', { headers: authHeaders });
    this.sessions = await resp.json();
  } catch (e) {}
},

newChat() {
  this.sessionId = null;
  this.sessionCwd = null;
  this.messages = [];
  this.sidebarOpen = false;
},

async selectSession(s) {
  this.sessionId = s.session_id;
  this.sessionCwd = s.cwd || null;
  this.messages = [];
  this.sidebarOpen = false;
  try {
    const resp = await fetch(`api/sessions/${s.session_id}/messages`, { headers: authHeaders });
    const history = await resp.json();
    for (const m of history) {
      if (m.role === 'user') {
        this.messages.push({ type: 'user', content: m.content });
      } else {
        this.messages.push({ type: 'assistant', blocks: m.blocks || [{ type: 'text', content: m.content || '' }] });
      }
    }
    this.$nextTick(() => this.scrollToBottom());
  } catch (e) {}
},

scrollToBottom() {
  const el = this.$refs.messages;
  if (el) el.scrollTop = el.scrollHeight;
},
fileToBase64(file) {
  return new Promise((resolve) => {
    const reader = new FileReader();
    reader.onload = () => {
      const b64 = reader.result.split(',')[1];
      resolve({ media_type: file.type || 'image/png', data: b64 });
    };
    reader.readAsDataURL(file);
  });
},

async addFiles(files) {
  for (const f of files) {
    if (f.type.startsWith('image/')) {
      this.pendingImages.push(await this.fileToBase64(f));
    }
  }
},

async sendMessage() {
  const text = this.prompt.trim();
  const images = this.pendingImages.slice();
  this.prompt = '';
  this.pendingImages = [];
  this.sending = true;

  this.messages.push({ type: 'user', content: text, images: images.length ? images : null });
  const assistantMsg = { type: 'assistant', content: '', loading: true, elapsed: 0 };
  this.messages.push(assistantMsg);
  const msgIdx = this.messages.length - 1;

  const timer = setInterval(() => { assistantMsg.elapsed++; }, 1000);
  try {
    const resp = await fetch('api/chat', {
      method: 'POST',
      headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json', ...authHeaders },
      body: JSON.stringify({ prompt: text, session_id: this.sessionId, cwd: this.sessionCwd, images: images.length ? images : undefined }),
    });

    if (!resp.ok) {
      throw new Error(`HTTP ${resp.status}: ${resp.statusText}`);
    }

    const reader = resp.body.getReader();
    const decoder = new TextDecoder();
    let buffer = '';

    while (true) {
      const { done, value } = await reader.read();
      if (done) break;
      buffer += decoder.decode(value, { stream: true });

      const lines = buffer.split('\n');
      buffer = lines.pop();

      let eventType = null;
      for (const line of lines) {
        if (line.startsWith('event: ')) {
          eventType = line.slice(7);
        } else if (line.startsWith('data: ') && eventType) {
          const data = JSON.parse(line.slice(6));
          if (eventType === 'text') {
            this.messages[msgIdx].content += data;
          } else if (eventType === 'error') {
            this.messages.push({ type: 'error', content: data });
          } else if (eventType === 'cancelled') {
            this.messages[msgIdx].content += '\n\n*[Cancelled]*';
          } else if (eventType === 'done') {
            this.sessionId = data;
            this.loadSessions();
          }
          eventType = null;
        }
      }
    }
  } catch (err) {
    this.messages.push({ type: 'error', content: err.message });
  }
  clearInterval(timer);
  this.messages[msgIdx].loading = false;
  this.sending = false;
},
async cancelQuery() {
  await fetch('api/cancel', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: authHeaders,
  });
},
  };
}
</script>

</body>
</html>

Serving the page

The app is meant to be installed as a PWA on phones and tablets — that way it feels like a native app rather than a browser tab. This requires a web manifest, icons, and a service worker on the backend, and a properly structured HTML shell that the browser can install.

HTML shell

The layout follows a standard messaging app pattern: sidebar for navigation, main area for the conversation, input bar pinned to the bottom. The sidebar is always visible on desktop but hidden behind a hamburger menu on mobile to maximize screen real estate for the conversation.

Both third-party scripts (Tailwind CSS, Alpine.js) are pinned to exact versions and loaded with Subresource Integrity (SRI) hashes. This matters more here than in a typical web app: a compromised CDN script runs with full page privileges, meaning it could read the app token from the meta tag and send commands to Claude Code via /api/chat — resulting in arbitrary code execution on the server (permissions are bypassed).

SRI alone is not enough though. It pins the hash, but if the file was already backdoored when we pinned it, we just locked in the backdoor. To address this, both packages are sourced from npm — where they can be cross-verified across independent CDNs (jsdelivr, unpkg) and the npm registry tarball. A verification script checks all three sources agree before an upgrade. The Tailwind v3 play CDN (cdn.tailwindcss.com) was replaced with @tailwindcss/browser for this reason: the play CDN was only served from one source, making independent verification impossible.

PWA assets and routes

The icons are generated procedurally to avoid shipping binary assets. The service worker provides basic offline caching so the shell loads instantly even on flaky connections.

@app.route("/manifest.json")
async def manifest():

        ],
    })
    return Response(m, mimetype="application/manifest+json")


def _generate_icon_png(size):
    """Generate a simple PNG icon with a 'C' letter on dark background."""
    import struct, zlib
    # Create RGBA image
    pixels = bytearray()
    cx, cy, r = size // 2, size // 2, size // 2 - 2
    bg = (0x1a, 0x1a, 0x2e, 0xff)
    fg = (0x0f, 0x34, 0x60, 0xff)
    for y in range(size):
        pixels.append(0)  # PNG filter byte
        for x in range(size):
            dx, dy = x - cx, y - cy
            dist = (dx * dx + dy * dy) ** 0.5
            if dist <= r:
                # Draw a "C" shape: outer ring minus right opening
                inner_r = r * 0.55
                if dist >= inner_r and not (dx > 0 and abs(dy) < inner_r * 0.5):
                    pixels.extend(fg)
                else:
                    pixels.extend(bg)
            else:
                pixels.extend(bg)
    # Encode as PNG
    def _png_chunk(chunk_type, data):
        c = chunk_type + data
        return struct.pack(">I", len(data)) + c + struct.pack(">I", zlib.crc32(c) & 0xffffffff)
    header = b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n"
    ihdr = _png_chunk(b"IHDR", struct.pack(">IIBBBBB", size, size, 8, 6, 0, 0, 0))
    idat = _png_chunk(b"IDAT", zlib.compress(bytes(pixels)))
    iend = _png_chunk(b"IEND", b"")
    return header + ihdr + idat + iend

      <text x="50" y="68" text-anchor="middle" font-size="60" font-family="sans-serif"
            font-weight="bold" fill="#e94560">C</text>
    </svg>'''
    return Response(svg, mimetype="image/svg+xml")

@app.route("/icon-512.png")

@app.route("/sw.js")
async def service_worker():
    sw = """\
const CACHE = 'claude-v2';
const PRECACHE = ['icon.svg', 'icon-192.png', 'icon-512.png'];

self.addEventListener('install', e => {
  e.waitUntil(caches.open(CACHE).then(c => c.addAll(PRECACHE)));
  self.skipWaiting();
});

self.addEventListener('activate', e => {
  e.waitUntil(caches.keys().then(ks => Promise.all(
    ks.filter(k => k !== CACHE).map(k => caches.delete(k))
  )));
  self.clients.claim();
});

self.addEventListener('fetch', e => {
  if (e.request.method !== 'GET') return;
  e.respondWith(
    fetch(e.request).catch(() => caches.match(e.request))
  );
});
"""
    return Response(sw, mimetype="application/javascript")


@app.route("/healthz")
async def healthz():
    return "ok"


@app.route("/")
async def index():
    token = secrets.token_urlsafe(32)
    now = time.time()
    # Expire after 24 h; prune old tokens
    app_tokens[token] = now + 86400
    expired = [t for t, exp in app_tokens.items() if exp < now]
    for t in expired:
        del app_tokens[t]
    return await render_template("index.html", app_token=token)

    app.run(debug=os.environ.get("DEBUG", "1").lower() in ("1", "true"), host="0.0.0.0", port=port)
